test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: When flushing a radiator, what is the purpose of submerging the radiator in a water tank after flushing?

options.text: To check for leaks using air pressure
To refill the radiator with coolant
To clean the exterior of the radiator

solution:
The correct answer is __To check for leaks using air pressure__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Submerging the radiator__ in a water tank after flushing helps detect any leaks effectively.
 
• This process involves using air pressure to identify areas where air bubbles escape, indicating a leak.
 
• It ensures that the radiator is sealed properly and safe for use after maintenance.
 
• Checking for leaks at this stage prevents future damage or overheating issues in the vehicle.
 
• This method is a standard practice in automotive maintenance and repair.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Purposes for Radiator Maintenance:**

 
 
• Flushing the radiator removes dirt, rust, and debris to ensure optimal performance.
 
• It helps in maintaining the engine temperature by ensuring proper coolant flow.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Using Proper Tools:**
 
 
• Specialized equipment like air pressure testing kits are used for this process.
 
• Using the right tools ensures accurate diagnostics and avoids damage to the radiator.
